note: GDPR submodule that defines an Anonymizer PLUGIN TYPE (manager plugin.manager.anonymizer, namespace Plugin/Anonymizer, annotation @Anonymizer, interface AnonymizerInterface, base AnonymizerBase) plus 10 built-in plugins (email_anonymizer, username_anonymizer, text_anonymizer, long_text_anonymizer, random_text_anonymizer, number_anonymizer, date_anonymizer, password_anonymizer, uri_anonymizer, clear_anonymizer) and services anonymizer.faker + anonymizer.anonymizer_factory. It has NO config, UI, routes, permissions or Drush - it is a plugin library. Because it stores no config, the medium case is a live-plugin-manager introspection (no config to write); the hard case exercises the real extension point by adding a custom @Anonymizer plugin (a small custom module) and checking the plugin manager discovers it. HARD teardown uninstalls the test module before deleting its directory (an orphaned enabled module fatals the kernel).

evals.prompt: The Drupal GDPR 'anonymizer' submodule lets you add your own anonymization strategy. What plugin type does it define - the manager service, plugin namespace, annotation, and base class?
evals.expected_output: An Anonymizer plugin type: manager service plugin.manager.anonymizer, plugin namespace Plugin/Anonymizer, annotation @Anonymizer, interface AnonymizerInterface, base class AnonymizerBase. Plugins implement anonymize($input, $field=NULL).

evals.prompt: Which anonymizer plugin does the GDPR anonymizer module provide for email addresses, and name a few other built-in anonymizers. Which library generates the fake values?
evals.expected_output: email_anonymizer (returns faker->unique()->safeEmail). Others include username_anonymizer, text_anonymizer, long_text_anonymizer, random_text_anonymizer, number_anonymizer, date_anonymizer, password_anonymizer, uri_anonymizer and clear_anonymizer. Values come from the Faker library via the anonymizer.faker service.

evals.prompt: In the GDPR anonymizer module, how do I get a Faker generator and how do I instantiate a specific anonymizer by id programmatically?
evals.expected_output: Use the anonymizer.faker service (FakerService::generator() returns a Faker\Generator) and the anonymizer.anonymizer_factory service (AnonymizerFactory::get($plugin_id) returns an anonymizer instance); the plugin manager is plugin.manager.anonymizer.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the anonymizer plugin manager and state which anonymizer plugin id would be used to anonymize an email address.
evals.expected_output: email_anonymizer - listed by plugin.manager.anonymizer->getDefinitions() on the live site (it returns a fake safeEmail).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a custom anonymizer to the GDPR anonymizer system: create and enable a small module providing an @Anonymizer plugin with id 'anonymizer_eval_static' (extending AnonymizerBase) whose anonymize() returns a fixed string, so it is discoverable by plugin.manager.anonymizer.
evals.expected_output: A custom module (e.g. under web/modules/custom) with src/Plugin/Anonymizer/StaticAnonymizer.php annotated @Anonymizer(id = "anonymizer_eval_static", ...) extending AnonymizerBase, enabled so plugin.manager.anonymizer->hasDefinition('anonymizer_eval_static') is TRUE. (Uninstall the module before deleting its directory.)
